name: Roll Your Own Poker
description: Roll Your Own is a strategic 'style' of Stud Poker (most commonly Seven-Card Stud) where the dealer provides cards face-down, and players choose which ones to reveal to their opponents. This shifts the game from a test of luck into a nuanced game of information management and bluffing. 'Dakota' is a specific high-low variation of this style featuring personal wild cards based on the lowest hidden card.

overview.description: Roll Your Own is a strategic 'style' of Stud Poker (most commonly Seven-Card Stud) where the dealer provides cards face-down, and players choose which ones to reveal to their opponents. This shifts the game from a test of luck into a nuanced game of information management and bluffing. 'Dakota' is a specific high-low variation of this style featuring personal wild cards based on the lowest hidden card.

history.origins: Developed as a home-game enhancement to Seven-Card Stud. It gained popularity in rural American poker circles (like North/South Dakota, giving rise to the 'Dakota' variant) for adding a 'choice' element to the otherwise fixed Stud deal.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Variations of Mexican Stud and Roll-Your-Own begin appearing in gambling guides.
1970s-90s: Becomes a staple of 'Dealer's Choice' home games.
Modern: Frequently played with local house rules like 'low-hole' wild cards.
history.cultural: Typically a 'kitchen table' or 'social club' game rather than a casino tournament standard, prized for the tension of the simultaneous 'reveal' phase.
history.evolution: The game evolved into several regional distinct variants: Mexican Stud (5-card), Mississippi Mud (7-card discard), and Dakota (Wild Card Hi-Lo).

setup.dealing: Varies by variant. Standard 'Roll Your Own' deals 3 cards down initially, then 4 more sequentially.
setup.equipment: Standard cards, poker chips, dealer button.

rules.objective: Form the best 5-card poker hand out of 7 dealt cards to win the pot.
rules.gameplay: 1. Ante/Blinds. 2. Deal 3 cards face-down. 3. Players simultaneously 'roll' (reveal) one card. 4. Betting round. 5. Deal 4th card down; players reveal one of their hidden cards. 6. Repeat for 5th and 6th cards. 7. Deal 7th card down. 8. Final betting round and Showdown.
keyRules: Reveals must be simultaneous (usually on a count of 'one-two-three-flip').
You cannot look at the card you just received before choosing which one to flip (in strict variants).
Once a card is rolled, it remains face-up for the duration of the hand.

strategy.basic: Keep your best cards (Aces, potential pair partners) hidden as long as possible. Reveal cards that make you look weak to induce bluffs, or reveal scary cards to push people out.
strategy.intermediate: In Dakota, 'buying the option' is essential if you have a powerful wild card (like an Ace as your low-hole) and don't want to risk a Deuce or Three 'replacing' it as the wild rank.
strategy.advanced: Information suppression: if you roll a Jack and have another Jack hidden, you are 'representing' a pair but keeping the strength concealed. If you roll two disparate cards, you look like you are chasing a flush/straight.
tips: Observe which cards opponents choose to reveal first; cautious players reveal their lowest 'junk' cards.
In Hi-Lo variants, always track the number of low cards showing to judge the safety of a low-hand split.
The choice of what to reveal is your primary weapon - use it to tell a story.

variations.name: Mexican Stud
variations.description: Five-card version. Two down initially, roll one. Dealt one down, roll one, until 4 up 1 down.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses different hand size and deal pattern; overrides to be added when implementing.

variations.name: Mississippi Mud
variations.description: Two cards discarded from 7. Every card is revealed sequentially. High-Low with declaration.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses discard and declaration; overrides to be added when implementing.

scoring.description: Standard Poker hand rankings (Royal Flush down to High Card). Dakota uses Hi-Lo split.

synthesis.shortDescription: A tactical upgrade to Seven-Card Stud. Instead of the dealer deciding what's face-up, you do. Hide your power, bluff your weakness, and in the Dakota variant, let your lowest card go wild.
